title: TAPE: A Biodegradable Hemostatic Glue Inspired by a Ubiquitous Compound in Plants for Surgical Application
protocol: Place a 4 ml-sized glass vial on a magnetic stirrer.
Add 1 ml of distilled water with a stirring bar to the vial.
Add 1 g of tannic acid to the vial.
Dissolve tannic acid in water by gentle stirring at 200 rpm for more than 1 hour.
Vortex mix 1 g of PEG powder (4-arms, 10 kDa) and 1 ml of distilled water to form a white slurry.
Incubate the PEG slurry at 60 °C for 10 minutes until it becomes clear.
Vortex mix 1 g of linear PEG powder (4.6 kDa) and 1 ml of distilled water to form a white slurry.
Incubate the linear PEG slurry at approximately 58 °C for 10 minutes until it becomes clear.
Mix 329 µl of the PEG (4-arms, 10 kDa) solution with 671 µl of the TA solution in a micro-centrifuge tube.
Gently blend the two viscous and honey-like solutions to mix them homogeneously.
Spin the mixture at 12,300 x g for 3 min in a centrifuge equipped with a fixed-angle rotor.
Carefully remove as much of the supernatant as possible using a micropipette.
Collect the product that has settled down; this is the fully formed TAPE.
Store the TAPE in the refrigerator (4 - 8°C) for up to several weeks.
Prepare two pieces of porcine skin tissue with a diameter of 6 mm by cutting them after removing all fat from the skin tissue.
Apply commercial cyanoacrylate glue to the outer side of each tissue.
Attach the tissue to the metallic rod.
Apply a drop of TAPE to one side of the tissue.
Spread the TAPE uniformly using another tissue on their inner sides.
Manually attach and detach the two sides of tissues several times.
Carefully grip each side of the rod with the UTM.
Apply a force of 20 N for 1 min.
Pull each rod in an opposite direction at a rate of 1 mm/min until the tissues are completely detached.
Add 20 µl of water on the detached area between two tissues.
Attach the tissues immediately after adding water.
Perform the detachment test again with the machine.
Cut a cap (d = 8 mm) of micro-centrifuge tube.
Weigh the cap to define it as Wc.
Fill the cap with 150 mg of TAPE.
Weigh the cap with TAPE together again to set it as a total initial weight W0.
Place the cap containing TAPE into a cell culture flask (75 cm2).
Add 50 ml of PBS buffer (1x, pH 7.4) to the cell culture flask so that the TAPE in the cap is completely immersed.
Incubate the cell culture flask in an orbital shaking incubator at 37 °C with gentle stirring (50 rpm).
Take the cap with TAPE from the cell culture flask.
Dry them by blowing nitrogen gas.
Weigh the cap containing remaining TAPE to determine Wt.
Replace the fresh PBS buffer and shake again after measuring Wt at each time point.
Calculate the relative remaining weight (%) using the equation: Relative remaining weight (%) = (Wt - Wc)/(W0 - Wc) x 100%
Anesthetize mice with an intraperitoneal injection of tiletamine-zolazepam (33.333 mg/kg) and xylazine (7.773 mg/kg).
Confirm proper anesthetization by pinching the paw gently and observing movements; no movement indicates sufficient anesthesia.
Apply vet ointment to the eyes while under anesthesia to prevent dryness.
Expose the liver via a midline abdominal incision.
Prick the liver with an 18 G needle to induce bleeding.
Remove flowing blood with sterile gauze.
Put 100 µl of TAPE or fibrin glue immediately on the bleeding site for positive control.
Place a filter paper underneath the liver to collect blood from the damage site.
Replace the filter paper with a fresh one every 30 seconds for four times (2 minutes).
Measure the mass of absorbed blood on each filter paper collected every 30 seconds.
Sacrifice mice through CO2 asphyxiation euthanasia after the animal experiment.
